{"edits": [{"finding_ids": ["app/profiles.py:8:optional-no-default", "app/profiles.py:9:optional-no-default", "app/profiles.py:10:optional-no-default", "app/profiles.py:15:test-failure"], "search": "    bio: Optional[str]
    website: Optional[str]
    age: Optional[int]", "replace": "    bio: Optional[str] = None
    website: Optional[str] = None
    age: Optional[int] = None", "explanation": "In Pydantic v1, a bare Optional[X] annotation implied a default of None. In Pydantic v2 such fields are required, so the form-based constructor in profile_from_form fails when blank values are filtered out of the input (bio missing -> 'Field required'). Adding explicit `= None` restores the v1 behavior, as described in the Pydantic v2 migration guide ("Required, optional, and nullable fields"). This same change resolves the test failure at line 15, since the failing test omits bio and the other blank fields from the input dict."}], "notes": "Single edit covers all three optional-no-default findings (lines 8-10) and the test-failure finding at line 15. The test failure is caused by the same root cause: profile_from_form drops blank/None values before calling Profile(...), so the now-required Optional fields raise 'Field required'. Adding `= None` makes them optional with a default of None, matching v1 semantics. No import changes needed: Optional is already imported and still used. The `interests: List[str] = []` field is already valid in v2 (Pydantic copies mutable defaults), so it was left unchanged. No other v1 APIs appear in this file. Documentation was not retrieved; the rationale relies on the documented v2 required/optional field behavior."}
